title: "Performance & Reliability"
---

IrisPipe is validated by two GitHub Actions workflows:

- **k6 Benchmark** measures runtime latency and API throughput on a CI runner.
- **Backend K6 Checks** runs regression suites against a real Spring Boot backend.

## What the Benchmark Measures

The benchmark workflow starts the real backend and runs both `backend/k6/benchmark.js` and `backend/k6/data-volume-benchmark.js`.
It validates:

1. Synchronous pipeline execution latency plus API latency/request rate
2. H2 → H2 JOB vs CHUNK timing and rows/s at 1,000 / 10,000 / 100,000 rows
3. 10,000-row failure semantics: JOB rolls back the whole job while CHUNK preserves previously committed chunks
4. PostgreSQL → H2 10,000-row cross-database JDBC paths for both JOB and CHUNK

All performance values are repeatable GitHub Actions CI-runner regression benchmarks, not production-capacity claims.

---

## Test Strategy

k6 is used for **integration-level correctness**, not only synthetic load generation.
Each regression suite:

1. Boots the real Spring Boot backend from a compiled jar
2. Runs API flows that exercise a specific behavioral domain
3. Asserts on status codes, response shape, persisted state, and runtime transitions
4. Tears down cleanly

This gives stronger coverage than controller-only tests for runtime semantics because it exercises the stack:
controller → service → Spring Batch → database.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  P["Push / workflow dispatch"] --> B["mvn package + unit tests"]
  B --> A["API / runtime benchmark"]
  B --> V["Data-volume matrix\nJOB / CHUNK × 1k / 10k / 100k"]
  B --> F["10k failure semantics\nJOB / CHUNK"]
  B --> X["PostgreSQL → H2\nJOB / CHUNK"]
  B --> R["10-suite k6 regression matrix"]

  A --> KP["Update performance-results.json"]
  V --> KP
  F --> KP
  X --> KP
  R --> RP["Update k6-regression-results.json"]

  KP --> Q["Render Quarto site"]
  RP --> Q
  Q --> D["Deploy GitHub Pages"]
```

## Benchmark Methodology

The benchmark workflow:

1. Runs `mvn package`, so backend unit tests are part of the gate
2. Builds one runnable jar and reuses it across benchmark jobs
3. Runs the API/runtime benchmark
4. Runs the H2 → H2 data-volume matrix at 1k / 10k / 100k rows for JOB and CHUNK
5. Injects a duplicate-key failure at 10k rows to verify large-volume transaction boundaries
6. Runs PostgreSQL → H2 at 10k rows for both atomicity modes
7. Aggregates JSON artifacts into `quarto/performance-results.json`
8. Regenerates the Quarto tables and deploys GitHub Pages
